items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: Bill Russell's real interested in Jelly Roll

ctx.x: Who was in Jelly Roll's band? I'm... Bill Russell's real interested in Jelly Roll, so I thought I'd ask you about it. But Russell wants to know all he can about Jelly Roll.
Well, I tell you, Jelly Roll had a band. Yeah, the fellow named... Was playing trumpet by the name of Melton.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: Eddie Garland and Bud Scott and Minor Hall, who was the younger brother of Tubby Hall.

ctx.x: Now these are typed in the back of the Defender notes.

Yeah. That's some of the later Defender notes, some things that I probably didn't get. He probably looked through my notes and then went up there and went through a couple of years. We'll copy all this stuff for you. So in any case, there are a few other interviews, people that are dead there like Tubby Hall and Joe Lindsay. Unfortunately, we got very little bit from Tubby Hall. I wanted to apologize on that. He was one of the great drummers, I'm convinced the more I hear of other drummers especially. At that…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Uh, uh, Ed Garland, Montuti, they call it. He was one of my very favorite musicians.

ctx.x: So, um, I did, uh, record that Roy Palmer I got on trombone and later Kid Ory on trombone. And, uh, um, St. Cyr, of course, and Pops Foster, several bass players. Uh, uh, Ed Garland, Montuti, they call it. He was one of my very favorite musicians. He still plays in California. Well, anyway, I have about 20 interviews, uh, different instruments. Natty Dominic, um, on trumpet. Bunk would have been a logical one. He was already dead. I never did get Louie. I would have tried to get him sometime, although it's a…
And this is on the New Orleans Ensemble Stock.
